newsitem.title: UK: ASDA to turn Co-op store into hypermarket.
newsitem.headline: ASDA to turn Co-op store into hypermarket.

text.p: ASDA Group Plc said on Wednesday it had bought one of the Co-operative Society's largest supermarkets for an undisclosed sum.

ASDA said in a statement that the Portsea Island Co-op superstore in Havant, Hampshire, in the south of England would "be an important addition to the 208 strong ASDA chain and will join its hypermarket division of very large destination stores".
An ASDA spokesman declined to comment on what ASDA was paying for the site, the building and the business of the large Havant site, which has an overall area of 140,000 square foot.
ASDA said the Havant store would continue to trade as a Co-op until November 4. It will be re-launched as an ASDA hypermarket on November 11 after refurbishment.
"All 364 full and part-time staff will be given the opportunity to become ASDA colleagues and more people are expected to be recruited to the store," ASDA added.
